subject: Next steps: SDK onramp & local pilot (auth, routing, embeddings)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Cortez <sofia@acmehealth.com>, Danielle Price <dani.price@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: SDK onramp & local pilot (auth, routing, embeddings)

Hi Sofia / Dani —

Thanks again for the call today. Great to meet the Acme Health team and hear about the prioritization around clinician-facing summarization and code/routing safety checks. Per our discussion, here are the concrete next steps to get a local pilot and quick SDK validation running this sprint: 

1) Distribute quickstart materials (attached) — we shared a short deck plus an environment checklist. Please review the checklist and confirm staging network constraints.

2) Technical kickoff & sample apps — we will hand you two minimal sample apps (Python and TypeScript) that show: auth via API key + optional JWT, per-request routing (tenant tag example), structured tool-calling output (function-style JSON), and embeddings + a reranker example for clinical note retrieval.

3) Sandbox access & IPs — tell us whether Acme needs fixed egress IPs or VPC peering. If you need IP allow-listing, share the CIDR range for staging so we can provision.

4) Data handling & KMS — confirm whether keys must be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for the pilot. We can default to Redwood-managed keys for initial testing.

5) Timeline — propose we aim to have the sample apps running locally and calling the sandbox by next Tuesday (2027-05-18). Can you confirm availability for a 30-min follow-up?

Deliverables from our side this week (Ben/Marissa/Karthik):
- Python/TS sample repos (local run instructions + unit tests)
- Short walkthrough doc for embedding + rerank baseline
- Staging connectivity checklist with IPs and KMS options

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-deck.pdf, acme-env-checklist.xlsx

If that all looks good, we’ll kick off the repo links and a calendar invite for Tuesday.

Thanks —
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

Thanks for the clear summary. This matches our internal notes. Quick answers inline:

- Staging network: we prefer fixed egress IPs for allow-listing. I’ll get the CIDR ranges from infra and share by EOD tomorrow.
- KMS: pilot prefers customer-managed keys scoped to PHI data stores; we can use Redwood-managed keys initially for dev, but will need KMS for the end-to-end test.
- Timeline: Tuesday 2027-05-18 at 10am PT works for our engineers (I’ll accept a calendar invite).

A couple of asks before the call:
1) Can you include a short README that shows how to run the TypeScript sample with local mocking of the embeddings endpoint?
2) For the reranker example, can you include expected embeddings dimensionality and a small sample dataset so we can sanity-check results locally?

We’re excited to get hands-on; Danielle will coordinate procurement touches (I copied procurement in case we need early paperwork).

Best,

Hi Sofia / team —

Quick technical notes ahead of the 10am PT call and the sample repo links (I’ll push these to the Drive and paste the links in the calendar invite):

Local run / sandbox guidance (high level):
- Python sample: clone repo, create virtualenv, pip install -r requirements.txt, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<sandbox-key>, python run_local.py --mock-embeddings (this launches a small Flask mock for embeddings + a test dataset).
- TypeScript sample: npm ci; npm run dev:start; env file example provided (.env.example) showing REDWOOD_API_KEY and optional JWT_PRIVATE_KEY for signed requests. The TS sample includes an express middleware that demonstrates routing by tenant (X-Redwood-Tenant header).

Auth & routing notes:
- We support API key auth and optional JWT bearer for workload identity. For the pilot, API key is simplest; we will provide a scoped sandbox key tied to the DEAL-2027-137 workspace.
- Routing example in TS demonstrates per-request model selector: if request.header['X-Route-To'] === 'low_cost' then route to model-variant: small-q4; otherwise use high-quality variant. 

Structured output / tool calling:
- Both samples include a function-calling example (schema-based JSON in the response) that the app parses (see samples/common/functions.md). The TS sample returns {"procedure_suggestion": {"name":"followup_test", "params":{...}}} to show structured parsing.

Embeddings & reranker specifics:
- Embedding dimensionality for the provided sample dataset: 1536. We include a 250-row CSV plus matching embeddings file for local reranking tests. The Python repo contains a simple sklearn-based cosine scorer and a small Jupyter notebook to visualize.

Attachments we’ll push to the Drive before the call: redwood-quickstart-deck.pdf, acme-env-checklist.xlsx, samples/python.zip, samples/ts.zip, reranker-sample-dataset.zip

If you have CI/CD requirements or an SSO flow to validate before we hand over the sandbox key, tell me and we’ll adjust. See you at 10am.

Thanks,
Karthik
